claims.text: Sequential solution treatment, rapid quenching, and sub-critical aging can induce coherent nanoscale B2-type precipitates in an FCC CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy.
The proposed processing can produce a hierarchical dual-phase microstructure in bulk structural high-entropy alloys.
The initial as-cast CrMnFeCoNi alloy is chemically homogeneous and single-phase FCC.
Solution treatment at 1200–1300 °C followed by rapid quenching retains a supersaturated solid solution.
Aging at 500–650 °C for 1–10 hours precipitates fine B2 or comparable ordered nanoprecipitates.
The treatment is applicable to bulk structural samples used from room temperature to approximately 600 °C.
Thermomechanical working refines the FCC grain structure.
The nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby provide precipitation strengthening.
Maintaining precipitate coherency avoids premature crack nucleation.
Grain refinement improves both strength and ductility by promoting uniform plastic deformation.
Interphase interfaces and a stiffness contrast between phases raise the effective Young’s modulus.
The dual-phase architecture enhances fracture resistance through crack deflection and bridging.
The treatment will increase yield strength by 20–30% relative to the as-cast single-phase state.
The treatment will increase ductility by 10–20% relative to the as-cast single-phase state.
The treatment will increase Young’s modulus by 5–10% relative to the as-cast single-phase state.
The treatment will increase fracture toughness relative to the as-cast single-phase state.
As-cast homogeneous single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys typically exhibit a strength–ductility trade-off and limited gains in elastic stiffness.
Excessive precipitate coarsening, improper aging, or high oxygen contamination can reduce ductility or cause embrittlement.
Benefits require precipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction to remain within an optimal range.

contradictions.description: The route is repeatedly called thermo-mechanical and grain refinement is attributed to thermomechanical working, but the specified intervention contains only solution treatment, quenching, and aging and gives no deformation or mechanical-working step.
